The apple tree: growth stages, planting and care

By Gafar Laiya, Gujarat Bio Organics · Updated 2026-11-25

An apple tree (Malus × domestica) is a deciduous temperate fruit tree. Commercial trees are grafted: the variety (such as Royal Delicious or Gala) is joined onto a rootstock that decides the tree's size and how soon it bears. Seedling rootstock trees bear after 6–8 years; dwarfing clonal rootstocks such as M.9 or MM.106 bear in 2–3 years (SKUAST-J, ICAR-CITH).

How an apple tree grows through the year

The tree needs winter cold (chilling hours below 7°C) to break dormancy evenly. Flower buds for next year form in June–August, while this year's fruit is sizing. That is why healthy summer leaves and the October urea-zinc-boron spray decide next year's crop.

StageWhenWhat to do
DormancyDec–FebChilling below 7°C; winter pruning
Silver tipFeb–MarHorticultural mineral oil 2% against scale and mite eggs
Green tipMarStart watching for scab
Tight cluster / pink budMar–AprBoron spray
Full bloomAprNo sprays at all; bees at work
Petal fallApr–MayPost-bloom nitrogen if fruit set is heavy
Pea (8–12 mm) and walnut sizeMay–JunFruit thinning; start calcium sprays
Summer sizing and bud formationJun–AugProtect the leaves; irrigate dry spells
HarvestJul–OctPick by starch-iodine test and firmness
Leaf fallOct–NovUrea + zinc + boron reload spray

How to plant an apple tree

  1. Buy clean, virus-indexed plants. Mosaic and stem pitting viruses silently stunt young orchards; NHB's Clean Plant Programme is indexing 535 apple samples across J&K, Himachal and Uttarakhand.
  2. Match the rootstock to the soil: M.9 only in deep, fertile, irrigated soil with a trellis; MM.106 only in well-drained, non-clay soil; MM.111 for drier, shallower hill soil. Rootstock guide.
  3. Never replant straight into an old apple pit. Shift pits to the old alleyways or treat for replant disease first (solarise or fallow, virgin topsoil, FYM, VAM, Trichoderma and Pseudomonas).
  4. Keep the graft union 15–20 cm above the soil to avoid collar rot, and plant on a slight mound where soil stays wet.
  5. Plant 25–33% pollinizers spread through the block.
  6. Mulch a 10–15 cm ring, kept 30 cm away from the trunk.

Apple tree care through the year

Prune in winter and paste every cut over 2.5 cm; feed by age in two or three splits; thin fruit at pea size; give 4–6 calcium sprays; irrigate in May–June and August–September dry spells; keep monsoon water off the trunk; and spray only by a university schedule. Why apple leaves turn yellow

  • Mottled, early-dropping leaves in July–August: often Marssonina blotch (diseases).
  • Bronze, silvery leaves in summer: European red mite; check with a 10× lens for red eggs.
  • Yellowing between the veins of older leaves, early drop: magnesium; 1–2% magnesium sulphate at walnut stage.
  • Small, crowded leaves in rosettes: zinc (little leaf); 0.5% zinc sulphate + 0.25% lime.
  • Sparse, small yellow leaves on the whole tree: check the roots for root rot.

Questions farmers ask

How long does an apple tree take to grow fruit?

6–8 years on seedling rootstock; 2–3 years on clonal rootstocks such as M.9 or MM.106.

Can I grow an apple tree from seed?

A seedling grows into a tree, but its fruit will not match the parent. Commercial trees are grafted onto rootstocks.

When is the best time to plant apple trees?

During winter dormancy, before bud break, so roots settle before spring growth (Himachal and Kashmir orchards plant in the dormant season).

Why is my apple tree not fruiting?

Too few pollinizers or bees, too little winter chill for the variety, heavy pruning that removes fruiting spurs, an off year after a heavy crop, or too much nitrogen pushing shoots.
